Circular Economy

The Zero-Fiat Surf School of Mossel Bay

Coaches, cooks, and lifeguards earn their livelihoods entirely in satoshis along South Africa's southern coast, while corporate payment networks quietly dilute their adoption metrics.

Western Cape Bureau

In the township of Kwanonqaba in Mossel Bay, a community initiative is demonstrating what a closed-loop bitcoin economy looks like when paper currency is completely absent from payroll. According to BitcoinEkasi, the project pays every single staff member without touching national tender.

yeah, we pay zero salaries in fiat. surf coaches, lifeguards, teachers, cooks, groundsmen, project lead, driver, gardener... no one that works for us earns any fiat. The initiative estimates that within the youth community and associated households, approximately 500 individuals now transact in satoshis on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis, with coaches earning salaries and young surfers earning activity rewards that flow directly into local spaza shops (c69d3794).

The organic adoption on South Africa's southern coast stands in sharp contrast to recent institutional marketing across the region. Reviewing retail developments this week, Blink Wallet pointed out that headline growth figures often mask a fundamental shift in composition: a major South African payment network published a 95% surge in transaction volume, yet the underlying system had quietly blended dollar-pegged tokens alongside bitcoin.

As Blink noted in their weekly review, “Crypto payments up” and “Bitcoin adoption up” are no longer the same sentence. While corporate processors absorb multi-asset rails, grassroots communities demonstrate that genuine circular liquidity is built on everyday wages rather than custodial payment gateways (1ac2cc92).

Client Architecture

Plaza Drops Secret Keys in 6,500-Line Overhaul

Desktop software developers move toward blind signing and hardware isolation to protect local endpoints.

Engineering Desk

A significant architectural shift is underway among client developers seeking to eliminate the vulnerability of storing persistent credentials in application memory. The creator of the native desktop client Plaza announced the completion of a major security refactor spanning more than 6,500 modifications.

advanced question: how do you use a desktop client without giving it your secret key? assume that you want to hold your key in your machine. … Plaza no longer holds a secret key. By offloading signature delegation to local hardware or dedicated background daemons, native applications remove private keys from the attack surface entirely (505ef92a).

Perspectives, World Dispatches & Readings

Sovereignty

The Accidental Cypherpunks Who Never Left On-Premises

Small enterprises that resisted cloud consolidation are suddenly vindicated as automated data harvesting escalates.

Commentary by heidi-E

So many people don’t realize that many small, medium businesses or orgs and many, many people have been self-sovereign all along. Never trusted the cloud. Not gonna store any of their information on someone else’s servers let alone Amazon/Google/Microsoft’s. Kept data and servers on-prem. Didn’t think of it as cypherpunk or self-sovereign or any kind of ideology rather than self-protection of their data. With the current wave of AI, none of them ever wanted their data going to OpenAI or Anthropic or China either. Not new, not punk :-). Just how a lot of orgs and people have always operated. Often called “luddites” or “behind”, for NOT utilizing cloud services. Now they/we look visionary.... (481c319a)
